newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end limit down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end limit down on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking kept pressure on CME lumber futures and prices ended mostly down the $10.00 per tbf limit after touching off technical sell stops in late dealings, traders said.
November closed limit down at $395.00 and January at $387.30 per tbf. March also finished down the daily limit with other months off $7.10 to $7.00 per tbf.

The profit taking developed after recent sharp gains and new contract highs Thursday in November and January. November met technical resistance on the early advance and prices then fell, traders said.
"The market had gone up seven days in a row and it's no surprise there was profit taking," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.
But Cunningham cited the continued strong tone to cash lumber which may spark renewed support next week. Cash sources were quoting spruce prices mostly around $420, he added.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $405 per tbf, up $17 from midweek and $27 above last Friday's quote. Gains came on strong consumption and speculation some Canadian mills have already met their annual quota for free export allotments.
